Subject: A free browser guide for IT
Preview text: Generate one how-to guide in your browser before considering a paid plan.

Generate your first IT guide for free

Hi there,

Start with a browser-based IT procedure that contains no credentials or sensitive data. Scribe’s free Basic plan generates a how-to guide in the browser, giving your team a concrete piece of documentation to assess.

Scribe is documentation and workflow-capture software built to generate step-by-step how-to guides. Use the finished guide to evaluate the format for a software setup, account configuration or another web-based support task.

You can generate that first browser guide without paying for a plan. Basic covers browser-based guide generation; capturing a procedure in a desktop application requires Pro or Enterprise.

Create a free Basic account and generate one non-sensitive browser guide. You’ll have a real result to consider before deciding where Scribe belongs in your documentation workflow.

Try Scribe Basic free → https://scribehow.com/signup?plan=free

- Scribe

asset_metadata.single_idea: Instead of writing one browser-based IT procedure from scratch, walk through it in Scribe and let the free Basic plan generate a how-to guide your team can share.

selected_brief.selection_reason: This is the strongest supported first-use proposition for an IT buyer: it connects a concrete documentation task to an immediately available free plan without assuming an organization-wide rollout or paid commitment.

value_case.reader_benefit: If a useful IT procedure currently lives in someone's head, the team can turn one browser-based walkthrough into a guide others can use and share.
value_case.mechanism: On the free Basic plan, the user performs the procedure in the browser and Scribe generates a how-to guide from the steps.
decision_conditions: The free Basic workflow is limited to procedures performed in the browser.
Capturing desktop-application procedures requires Pro or Enterprise.

claim_conditions: Frame the undocumented-procedure situation conditionally; it is not established for every recipient.
Keep the proposed first use to a procedure performed in a web application.
Basic is free; desktop capture requires Pro or Enterprise.
Free Basic account; guide generation happens in the browser by manually performing the steps (E1)
Procedure must be performed in a web application, since desktop capture is a Pro or Enterprise feature (E5)
Do not promise: No claim that the team can scale documentation organisation-wide without a paid plan
Do not promise: No claim of zero disruption to current ticket or wiki practice
Do not promise: No claim of avoided or reduced headcount
Do not promise: No claim of replacing or outperforming an incumbent documentation tool
Do not promise: No claim that guides stay current automatically or feed internal AI tools
Do not promise: No time-saved or error-reduction promise applied to this buyer

This is a documented-use draft, not proof of the broader audience hypothesis or recipient fit.

Problem P1 is an inferred audience hypothesis: Some staff at technology companies report that unwritten, undocumented knowledge ('tribal knowledge') held by individuals is common and seen as important, with documentation often not treated as a first-class deliverable. Use it only conditionally (if this is relevant to the reader), not as a known current pain, behavior or outcome of the recipient. Product fit does not establish current demand or a demonstrated customer outcome.
Historical sources (2019-07-31); present applicability is not corroborated.
Single-source problem; independent corroboration is not established.
